gloss: landscape; scenery of mountains and water; landscape painting

definitions.gloss: landscape; scenery of mountains and water
definitions.explanation: The natural scenery formed by mountains and rivers. An aesthetic concept central to East Asian art and garden design.
A genre of East Asian painting depicting mountains, rivers, and natural landscapes. Abbreviated from 山水画.

examples.japanese: {美|うつく}しい{山水|さんすい}の{風景|ふうけい}。
この{庭園|ていえん}は{山水|さんすい}をかたどった{枯山水|かれさんすい}だ。
examples.english: This garden is a dry landscape that represents mountain and water scenery.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{山水|さんすい}は{四季|しき}ごとに{表情|ひょうじょう}を{変|か}える。
examples.english: Japan's natural landscape changes its appearance with each season.

examples.japanese: {水墨|すいぼく}の{山水|さんすい}を{描|えが}く。
examples.english: To paint a landscape in ink wash.

examples.japanese: {雪舟|せっしゅう}は{山水画|さんすいが}の{名手|めいしゅ}として{知|し}られる。
examples.english: Sesshu is known as a master of landscape painting.

examples.japanese: {中国|ちゅうごく}から{伝|つた}わった{山水画|さんすいが}は、{日本|にほん}で{独自|どくじ}の{発展|はってん}を{遂|と}げた。
examples.english: Landscape painting, which came from China, developed in its own unique way in Japan.

notes:
Composed of {山|さん} (mountain) + {水|すい} (water). A foundational concept in East Asian aesthetics representing the ideal natural landscape. The word evokes both actual scenery and artistic depictions of it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {山水画|さんすいが}: landscape painting (the full term)
- {枯山水|かれさんすい}: dry landscape garden — a rock garden that symbolizes mountains and water without using actual water
- {山水|さんすい}の{風景|ふうけい}: mountain-and-water scenery
- {水墨|すいぼく}{山水|さんすい}: ink-wash landscape

CULTURAL NOTE:
{枯山水|かれさんすい} (dry landscape) gardens, found at Zen temples like {龍安寺|りょうあんじ}, use rocks, gravel, and moss to abstractly represent {山水|さんすい} without water. This is one of the most iconic forms of Japanese garden design.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {風景|ふうけい}: scenery, landscape — general term for any view or scenery, without the cultural/artistic nuance
- {景色|けしき}: scenery, view — everyday word for what you see when looking at nature
- {山河|さんが}: mountains and rivers — more literary; emphasizes the physical geography of a land
